# The World's Lies

> "Be careful that you don't let anyone rob you through his philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men"
>
> — Colossians 2:8

The flesh supplies the itch. The world supplies the reasons to scratch it.

Two things keep a man in this trap. The first is the flesh, with its small, restless itch. I called that itch the Little Monster. The second is the lies, and they are much the bigger of the two. Call them the Big Monster. The Little Monster is tiny. The Big Monster is everything you've been told about him.

Your grandfather was told that this habit would make him go blind, grow hair on his palms and land him in an asylum. That was nonsense, and it deserved to be laughed out of the room. But when the scare stories went, the truth went out with them. The pendulum swung all the way over, and now a boy hears the opposite sermon, preached just as confidently. Here are its main points.

**"Everyone does it."** Nearly true. But a crowded trap is still a trap. Ask any man in it whether he would start again, and he'll say, "Not a chance." Since when did you take your direction from a crowd that's lost?

**"It's healthy. It's harmless. Doctors say so."** Medicine says it doesn't hurt your body, and I won't argue. But the doctor is answering a question you never asked. You didn't ask whether it would damage your prostate. You asked why you can't stop, and why you feel like a smaller man afterward. A Christian writer made the distinction neatly: "But just because something isn't harmful physically doesn't mean it's not harmful spiritually."

**"It's natural."** So is a great deal that you wouldn't copy. One preacher, who was bound by this for years himself, answers in nine words: "We also see in nature where pigs eat trash." That a thing occurs in nature tells you nothing about whether it's good for a man.

**"A man needs the release."** You need air, water and food. Go without those and you die. No man has ever been carried out of a tent after a week's camping because he couldn't get a minute alone.

**"It keeps you out of worse trouble."** Nowhere does the Bible tell a man to commit one sin in order to avoid another. And it doesn't even work. Ask the men who quit porn, kept the habit, and found that it let porn back in.

## The lies about porn and about women {-}

The world has a second set of lies for the screen, and a third for real women. Take the screen first.

**"Porn is just entertainment. Nobody gets hurt."** Somebody always does. You can't know whether the woman on the screen wanted to be there. You can't check her age, and you can't check whether she agreed. The sites haven't checked either. In 2020 a New York Times report found videos of rape and of underage girls on the biggest porn site in the world. The big card companies stopped handling its payments. Within days the site took down nearly ten million videos, because it had never checked who uploaded them.

Here is one case out of many. A company in California promised young women that their videos would never go online, and then put them on the free sites, where they were watched millions of times. In 2025 its owner was sentenced to twenty-seven years in prison for sex trafficking.

Millions of ordinary men watched those videos. Not one of them thought he was watching a crime. And the man who watches is not a bystander. He is the customer. The video was made for him, and his visit pays for the next one. Nobody told him. He was sold it as harmless entertainment, and so were you. It never was.

Whoever she is, she is somebody's daughter. And when it is her own choice, she has been told a lie of her own: that her worth is her body, and that men's hunger is a way to make a living. What ruins the man who watches ruins the woman who is watched.

**"At least I've never paid for sex."** You have, though nobody told you so. In porn a woman is paid to have sex so that a man can get off. That is prostitution, with a camera between her and you. The man at the brothel door hands her the money. The man at the screen pays through the site, with a card or with his eyes, because the site sells his attention. Think of cocaine and crack. Cocaine was the rich man's drug. Crack is the same drug made cheap, and sold on every corner. Porn is the crack. It is the brothel made cheap, open all night, and sold in every pocket.

**"It isn't a real woman, so nobody is hurt."** This lie arrived in the 2020s, when computers learned to make pictures and to talk. The picture was drawn, or a computer made it, or the girlfriend is a program. First, somebody often is hurt. Computers were soon being used to put real women's faces into porn they never made. One 2023 study counted nearly a hundred thousand of these fake videos online. Almost all of them were porn, and almost all the faces belonged to real women who never agreed to it. Second, even when no woman exists at all, you do. The thing being trained is your own heart, and it learns the same lesson from a drawing as from a photograph.

Now the lies about real women.

**"A real man gets as many women as he can."** That is the oldest lie of all. It makes a man's worth depend on being wanted, which is exactly what makes him easy to lead. A real man is one a woman can trust. Count how many of the men who live by the other rule you would trust with your sister.

There is a quieter version of the same man, and he would be insulted to be counted with the others. He buys the drinks, the dinner and the gift, and he isn't being kind. He is paying, and he knows what he hopes it will buy. Nothing is wrong with treating a woman well. The test is what you expect back. A gift wants nothing in return. A payment does.

**"It's only a little fun. She knew what it was."** Then why did you have to tell yourself so? Using a person is still using her when she agrees to it. Paul's rule, in his first letter to the Christians in Thessalonica, is short: "that no one should take advantage of and wrong a brother or sister in this matter". You already knew that. It is why it never felt like fun the next morning.

She has been lied to as well. She was told that sleeping with a man and expecting nothing from him is freedom. She was told that a pill makes it safe. She was told that if a child comes anyway, the child's life can be ended, as though that would cost her nothing. Nobody told her the price, and nobody asked what she was worth.

You don't have to take that from a church. In 2022 a British journalist named Louise Perry, who had worked at a rape crisis center, wrote a book arguing that the sexual revolution mostly served men who want sex without ties. One of her chapters is called "Consent Is Not Enough". And the regret shows when researchers ask. In one study of Canadian students in 2012, about three in four of those who had sex with no commitment said they had regretted it at some time, the men as well as the women.

So "she agreed" settles nothing. Men like to complain about women who have been with too many men. They never ask who those men were. If you slept with her and left, you were one of them. You helped to make the very woman you say you would never marry.

None of this is here to add to your guilt. It is here to take away the last excuse. You were lied to, and so was she. You don't need any of it, and it was never harmless.

## The quiet pulpit {-}

You'd expect the church to push back. Mostly it says nothing. A man can sit in a pew for thirty years and never hear this habit named once. A boy hears jokes about it at school and silence about it in church. He concludes that either it doesn't matter, or he must be the only one. Some kind and respected Christian teachers even said it was fine, to spare teenagers from crushing guilt.

## Two things to be fair about {-}

The people who defend the habit have two fair points, and I'll grant them both.

First, the Bible never mentions masturbation by name. If you were hoping for a verse that says "you shall not", there isn't one, and this book won't pretend there is. But Jesus didn't need to name the act, because he went behind it. In Matthew 5:28 he put the sin in the look and in the heart, and that is where this habit lives. Ask yourself how often it has happened without lust, and you have your answer. The Catholic Church goes further. It teaches that the act is wrong in itself, because sex was made to join a husband and wife. Many Protestant pastors reach the same place through Jesus's words about the look.

Second, the numbers. A psychiatrist who treats porn addiction estimates that about three in four of the men who watch it are not compulsive at all. He tells his audience so. He is talking about porn, and he means compulsive in the sense a clinic uses. I'll take his figure. This book has never said that every man who does this is a clinical addict. Its case rests on two things no clinic measures: what Jesus said about lust, and what men say the habit has cost them. Besides, you didn't pick up a book with this title because you were fine.

## The opposite lie {-}

There is hype in the other direction too. Whole corners of the internet promise great things if you stop. You'll get a deeper voice, clear skin, a surge of testosterone and women turning around in the street. The biggest forum of them all started with a thread about a study claiming a testosterone spike after seven days. That study has since been retracted. A sociologist put it flatly: "There is no scientific evidence that supports the idea of these superpowers."

Logically, all that hype ought to get men out. It doesn't. In fact it helps to keep them in, and that's why I call it a lie as well.

It turns stopping into a feat. You go on "hard mode", you count days and you call yourself a warrior. Every bit of that language tells you that you're giving up something enormous in exchange for a prize. Then day thirty comes, the prize hasn't arrived, and back you go.

It also leaves lust on the throne. "Quit so you can get women" only changes what the appetite is fed. Even the men I quote gratefully in this book sometimes sell it that way. Take their honesty about what the habit costs, and leave the sales pitch.

Both sermons, "it's good for you" and "quitting gives you powers", agree on one thing. They both say it's a big deal to stop. It isn't.

## The best liar of all {-}

The strangest thing is that the most persuasive voice in all this is your own.

Men in the trap aren't weak-willed. It takes real stamina to keep up a secret for twenty years. The trouble is where the strength goes. We pour it into defending the habit. Then, when we try to quit and fail, we turn it on ourselves. Failing at something is one thing. Hating yourself for it is another, and it leaks out into everything else. You stop going to the gym. The diet lasts until Thursday. Your children get the worst of your temper.

Nobody argues with himself about whether to give up golf. With this we argue every night, and we think that's normal.

So from now on, treat everything you've been told about this habit the way you'd treat a pushy salesman. Smile and nod, and don't sign. That goes for "you need it" and for "it's who you are". It also goes for the idea of a safe version. "Only in the shower", "only without a screen" and "only on weekends" were all invented by the Little Monster. Keep asking yourself two questions. "Why am I doing this? Do I actually need to?"

Of course you don't.

Once you're in the trap, the lies get help from inside. Some part of you knows the Little Monster expects feeding, and it will defend his dinner against any argument. That's fear: the fear of that empty, fidgety feeling.

Men believe they do it for pleasure or to relax, or because they have a high drive. The real reason is to quiet the Little Monster. The trap closes slowly. Most men don't know they're in it until the day they try to leave, and even then plenty won't admit it. Anyone who has raised the subject with a young man knows how the conversation goes:

"You know the only reason you keep doing it is that you can't stop?"

"Nonsense. I like it. If I didn't, I'd stop."

"Then stop for a month, just to show me."

"Why would I? I like it."

"Stop for a month to show yourself."

"There's no point. I told you, I like it."

He likes it so much that he won't risk finding out.

## "Giving up" {-}

One more thing keeps the lies standing. We never question them. We believe what we've always heard, most of all from the people we trust.

The world says the man who stops is missing out. So be clear about who is missing out. It isn't the man who stopped. It's the man who carries on. He hands over his energy, his time, his confidence and his peace of mind. And what does he get for it?

Nothing.

Each time, he gets the brief illusion of returning to the calm that the free man has all day long.

The phrase "giving up" is the plainest example of the lie. It smuggles in the idea of a sacrifice. But there's nothing to give up. You'll be getting rid of a parasite and gaining a great deal. So we'll drop that phrase here and now. In this book you don't "give up" lust. You stop. You quit. Best of all, **YOU ESCAPE.**

The world's lies are general. Your own are specific: this habit helps me with *this*, at *these* times. Those come next. We'll take the times you reach for it, one at a time.
